climbing_route.label: Dome Glacier to the 8,560 ft notch
climbing_route.notes: Rope up for the glacier crossing: follow roughly a 115° bearing up-glacier, working through visible crevasse bands, to a notch at ~8,560 ft just north of the summit block. Hazard named: the visible crevasse bands on the glacier.

climbing_route.label: Ingraham Glacier above Camp Muir
climbing_route.notes: Above Camp Muir (10,080 ft), traverse the heavily crevassed Ingraham Glacier — rope-team travel mandatory. A hard overnight freeze is essential for safe glacier travel.

climbing_route.label: Final 3,400 ft to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Start the summit push at 1-2 AM to climb the final 3,400 ft while snow is firm. Non-technical but exposed; the crux is route-finding through crevasse fields and steep snowfield sections.

climbing_route.label: Snow Creek Glacier basin to the east ridge saddle
climbing_route.notes: From Aasgard Pass head right/south along a short ridge above a tarn to reach Dragontail's east saddle, then cross the Snow Creek Glacier basin to the saddle on the east ridge. The basin is typically snow-covered through late July and is a mellow, low-crevasse slope.

climbing_route.label: East ridge to the summit
climbing_route.notes: A class-3 scramble/ridge walk along the east ridge from the saddle directly to the summit.

climbing_route.label: Gentle snow above Glacier Gap camp
climbing_route.notes: Summit day from the ~7,300 ft Glacier Gap high camp is roughly 5.25 mi with about 2,350 ft of gain and 835 ft of intermediate descent; it starts by climbing gentle snow above camp.

climbing_route.label: Volcanic scree onto the Gerdine and Cool glaciers
climbing_route.notes: Follow a climber's track on volcanic scree onto the Gerdine and Cool glaciers, end-running a crevasse or two.

climbing_route.label: Final steep pitch to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Rejoin the climber's trail for the final steep pitch to the summit.

climbing_route.label: West ridge crest
climbing_route.notes: From timber at the base of the west ridge, follow the timbered ridge itself up to where it opens onto rock and the class 3 scrambling begins. On the ridge proper, cairns mark a Class 3 line — stay LEFT (climber's left) on the crest; drifting right leads toward false summits and unintentional Class 4-5 terrain on loose, exposed rock.

climbing_route.label: Southwest basin and bergschrund
climbing_route.notes: An alpine start from the ~6,100 ft treeline camp gets the team into the southwest basin and across the bergschrund crux while it is still cold and firm.

climbing_route.label: X Couloir to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Roughly 1,500 ft of 30-40 degree snow plus a steep serac step in the X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit; the timing of the alpine start is what keeps this ground cold and firm.

climbing_route.label: West-side gullies back to the crest
climbing_route.notes: From the col, do not continue straight up the ridge crest - instead drop about 50 ft onto the west side of the ridge and climb one of several gullies (~100 ft) back up to the crest.

climbing_route.label: Ridge crest to the South Peak summit
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge over a mix of snow and blocky rock, with some exposure, to the South Peak summit.
